data_quality_assurance: Set up of scientific and technical committee
Use of tools for automatic checks
Consistency verified with data models and standards

We have implemented comprehensive documented procedures for quality assurance in our project "Healthcare Pathways of Heart Failure Patients within the Spanish National Health System and its Impact on Health Outcomes (CONCEPT-HF)." These procedures are designed to ensure the highest standards of data quality and reliability.
First, we have established a scientific and technical committee responsible for overseeing all aspects of data quality. This committee includes experts in data science, clinical research, and information technology, who provide guidance and oversight throughout the data collection and processing stages.
Second, we use advanced tools for automatic checks to identify and correct errors in the data. These tools perform validation checks to ensure that the data conforms to the specified format and meets predefined quality criteria. For instance, they check for missing values, outliers, and inconsistencies.
Third, our data is meticulously verified to conform to format specifications and consistency is checked against established data models and standards. This includes using standardized vocabularies like CDISC for clinical data and HL7 FHIR for healthcare data, ensuring interoperability and consistency.
Additionally, we conduct regular data audits and reviews to identify and rectify any discrepancies. All data processing steps are thoroughly documented, and version control systems are used to track changes, ensuring transparency and accountability.
By implementing these rigorous quality assurance procedures, we ensure that our data is accurate, reliable, and suitable for high-quality research and analysis.
dataset.description:
The CONCEPT-HF public health cohort links selected variables from primary care or hospital admission for Heart Failure (HF), covering a global population of approximately 19 million inhabitants for three regions of Spain (Andalucía, Aragón, País Vasco). This cohort includes all patients admitted to hospital due to HF in public hospitals and complementary information on patient attributes (i.e., comorbidities, healthcare system contacts, prescribed HF drugs) and patient health outcomes (i.e., readmissions and mortality). Original data is maintained and updated daily by the different health systems of each region described. A common data model specification with the required information to achieve the expected results of the research question is provided as supporting documentation
at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11234699 - Common Data Model Specification. Data is provided pseudonymised  and granted by the Andalusian Ethical Research Committee.
dataset.preservation_statement: Andalucía, Aragon and the Basque Country has a regional mandate to curate and maintain original data requests (and related ETL queries) in the long term and report on the re-use of health data for research purposes.

dmp.description:
This publication corresponds to the Data Management Plan (DMP) for "Care pathways of heart failure patients within the Spanish National Health System and its impact on health outcomes (CONCEPT-HF)" project.
The CONCEPT-HF project will introduce a novel concept, the healthcare trajectory, as an analytical tool for examining patient management in HF with the objective of identifying deviations that impact health outcomes and thus enabling the establishment of corrective measures. Given the substantial amount and variety of data to be analyzed, the use of process mining techniques will be indispensable to ensure the precision, consistency, and homogeneity necessary for robust and high-quality analysis.
A brief structured description of the research question, the proposed study design, and the cohort definition is provided below.

project.description:
The Carlos III Health Institute (ISCIII) is a public biomedical research institution in Spain, under the Ministry of Science and Innovation. Its main mission is to promote the generation of scientific knowledge in the field of health and encourage its application to improve the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases. Among its activities, the ISCIII manages and funds research projects to drive innovation and scientific advancement.

A competitively funded project is one that has obtained funds through a rigorous and competitive evaluation process. In this process, projects are assessed and selected based on their scientific quality, feasibility, relevance, and potential impact in the field of study. Projects selected for competitive funding must demonstrate excellence and the ability to significantly contribute to the advancement of knowledge and the improvement of public health.
